newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bean, corn acres this year highest since 80's.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bean, corn acres this year highest since 80's.

text.p: Responding to the highest soybean prices in almost 9 years and the least government involvement in more than 60 years, U.S. farmers are planning to plant 68.8 million acres of soybeans this year, the most U.S. bean acreage since 1980, the government said Monday.

In its first report on what American farmers will plant this spring, the Agriculture Department said a nationwide survey of 55,000 producers showed that farmers will plant 81.4 million acres of corn, the largest corn acreage in 12 years, as they take advantage of the new-found planting flexibility provided by last year's overhaul of U.S. farm policy.

The government's closely watched estimates -- released in the Agriculture Department's annual Prospective Plantings report -- also projected U.S. wheat plantings to be down across the board as farmers opted to plant the more profitable soybeans and corn.

Spring wheat and durum wheat plantings showed the biggest decreases at 17.8 million and 3.19 million acres respectively. Total U.S. wheat acreage this year is estimated at 69.2 million acres, down almost 10 percent from last year.
Cotton acreage is also anticipated to be down slightly at 14.5 million acres.
In 1996, farmers planted 64.2 million acres of soybeans, 79.5 million of corn, 75.6 million of wheat, 20.04 million of other spring wheat, and 14.67 million of cotton.

The government's soybean and corn acreage estimates were sharply above the expectations of commodity analysts and traders, and commodity prices at the Chicago Board of Trade were likely to drop as a result of the anticipated higher plantings and larger crops.
